evidence.title: Amp introduction
evidence.finding: Documents web, Apple apps, CLI and per-thread cloud Orbs.

evidence.title: Amp multiplayer
evidence.finding: Non-private Orb threads can enable time-limited shared prompting and environment access; owner pays.

evidence.title: Amp pricing
evidence.finding: Free product features with separate model/Orb costs, subscription and BYOK routes, thread cost detail.

evidence.title: Amp on iOS & macOS
evidence.finding: iOS app is available through TestFlight; macOS app is a direct download.

evidence.title: Introduction
evidence.finding: Amp offers web, macOS, iOS, Android and CLI access to threads; Orbs keep working after closing the laptop.

evidence.title: Pricing
evidence.locator: Amp tiers; How usage is charged; Enterprise; Notes
evidence.finding: Hobby includes product features with separately billed hosted Orbs and inference routes. Teams have no additional charge; enterprise pricing is custom.

evidence.title: Multiplayer
evidence.finding: Workspace members can co-prompt an enabled thread and access its Orb or shared runner; access is time-limited and bills the owner.

evidence.title: Modes & models
evidence.finding: Task and Read Thread subagents have separate context, report summaries and support follow-up work. They cannot communicate directly with one another.

evidence.title: GitHub & Git
evidence.finding: A GitHub App authorizes selected repositories, branches and PRs; events can continue a thread or spawn a new Orb.

evidence.title: Automations & webhooks
evidence.finding: A saved thread schedule wakes the same agent and Orb; one-off, recurring and completion-conditioned runs are documented.

evidence.title: MCP
evidence.finding: Amp manages local and remote MCP definitions with OAuth or headers; no external-tool call was tested.

evidence.title: AGENTS.md
evidence.finding: Repository, personal and managed guidance has documented inclusion scopes; workspace guidance excludes subagents, Puck and raw custom agents.

evidence.title: Orbs
evidence.locator: Orb spawn pacing; review; follow along
evidence.finding: Per-thread Orbs preserve files and services across idle pauses and queue starts beyond a documented burst allowance.

evidence.title: Sizes & costs
evidence.locator: Available sizes; Billing; When an Orb pauses
evidence.finding: Hosted sizes and hourly rates are published and billed by minute; idle pause stops charges. Enterprise self-hosted pricing changes after November 13.

evidence.title: Amp for Windows
evidence.finding: Experimental Windows 10 1809+/Windows 11 app for x64 and Arm. Threads and orbs, Windows notifications and taskbar actions are documented.

evidence.title: Threads
evidence.finding: Changes has per-commit diffs and navigation. Thread exports are Markdown or owner-only JSON. Artifacts are editable documents with revisions, conflict detection and Markdown/HTML/PDF export.

evidence.title: Shipping Changes
evidence.locator: Default Ship Flow; Ship Behavior; Restack Changes
evidence.finding: Default Ship commits, rebases, runs tests and pushes to the base branch. Push to Branch changes the destination; Custom Ship is a configurable prompt. Substantive conflicts require confirmation.

evidence.title: Customizing Orbs
evidence.finding: Project snapshots reuse dependencies up to 72 hours. Setup and resume scripts have distinct credentials and lifetimes. Services are declared separately; failed setup is visible in Setup Log.

evidence.title: Self-Hosted Orbs
evidence.locator: How It Works; Caution; infrastructure table
evidence.finding: An outbound provider runs user-supplied spawn/pause/delete dispatch. Docker and Kubernetes examples retain disk but not memory. Self-hosted Orbs still connect to Amp.

evidence.title: Runners
evidence.locator: Start a Runner; Create a Worktree
evidence.finding: Runners serve local or remote directories. New Worktree creates a sibling checkout and branch; threads can archive and remove only clean worktrees.

evidence.title: Workspaces
evidence.finding: Member uses shared resources; Admin also manages membership, billing, settings and policies and can inspect private threads. Enterprise adds narrower roles.

evidence.title: Amp Security Reference
evidence.locator: System Components; Data Security and Retention; Audit Logs; Assurance
evidence.finding: Amp describes a cloud control plane without self-hosted deployments, GCP storage, separately controlled training, thread deletion, SOC 2 Type II and authentication audit logs.

evidence.title: Amp Pricing
evidence.locator: Amp Tiers; How Usage Is Charged
evidence.finding: Hobby is recurring free with no included usage. BYO subscriptions/keys incur no Amp fees outside Enterprise. Megawatt costs $20/month with $20 usage and 750 a1.small Orb hours; compute and credits remain separate.

evidence.title: Amp License Terms
evidence.finding: Amp grants a revocable, nontransferable service license and reserves proprietary rights. This is a custom service license, not an open-source license.

evidence.title: Amp linux
evidence.locator: Linux app installation, local runner, tray and differences from Mac
evidence.finding: Amp has a native Linux desktop app with install instructions, desktop integration and a systemd-backed local runner. It supports tray operation and launch arguments; the Linux app lacks Mac Puck windows/dictation and multiple windows.

evidence.title: Amp models and subagents
evidence.locator: Introduction same agent everywhere; Models and Subagents main agent, custom agents and system models
evidence.finding: Amp uses its own agent across web, apps and CLI. The selected model is wrapped in Amp system prompts/tools; Task and Read Thread are Amp subagents. Custom plugin agents choose a model through amp.createAgent rather than selecting a third-party coding CLI harness.

evidence.title: Amp pricing
evidence.locator: Amp Tiers table; How Usage Is Charged; Enterprise. Page lastModified 2026-11-11.
evidence.finding: The complete public tier table lists Hobby free, Megawatt $20/month, Gigawatt $200/month, Teams at no additional charge and custom Enterprise. Usage and Orbs are separately metered. Members keep individual tiers; the public table has no separate per-seat workspace fee or one-time license.

desktop_os.answer: Amp offers macOS and an experimental Windows app. Windows requires Windows 10 1809 or Windows 11, with x64 and Arm builds; Linux desktop-client availability is not stated.

task_actions.answer: The Windows app starts threads in Orbs or on runners; its share action sends files or text to Puck. Client parity beyond the documented Windows basics remains unknown.

notifications.answer: Windows notifications report a thread ready for input, mentions and access requests; access requests can be answered in the notification.

plans.answer: Thread artifacts can hold plans and checklists, persisted with the thread. This does not establish acceptance gates.

editors.answer: Humans and agents edit the same artifact.

revisions.answer: Each artifact save creates a revision.

amendment.answer: Agents merge against a newer artifact revision when a concurrent save prevents their update.

persistent_requirements.answer: Artifacts can retain a plan or requirements document with a thread; a dedicated executable requirements schema is not established.

human_edits.answer: Workspace users allowed to open the thread can edit its artifacts.

agent_edits.answer: Every selectable agent mode can read and write artifacts using the artifact tool.

revisions.answer: Every artifact save creates a new revision.

later_retrieval.answer: Artifacts remain accessible from the thread Artifacts view until deleted.

byo_remote.answer: Users can supply their own Orb compute through amp orb provider and a dispatch program.

self_hosted.answer: Orb execution can be hosted on user infrastructure; this is not self-hosting the Amp control plane.

branch.answer: Runner worktree creation also creates a named branch.

worktree.answer: A runner creates a Git worktree and branch for a new thread; worktrees separate files without asserting a security sandbox.

container.answer: A documented Docker provider example runs each Orb as a container; this is a self-hosted execution option.

process.answer: Docker-backed Orbs do not preserve memory across pause; terminals and desktop processes are lost on wake.

code_separation.answer: Each runner worktree has its own working files and branch.

service_restart.answer: Docker-backed Orb services restart when a portal is reopened after wake; terminal and desktop process state is not restored.

context_loss.answer: Docker-backed Orbs retain disk but lose terminal and desktop process state when paused.

caches.answer: A matching prepared project snapshot is reused for up to 72 hours.

snapshots.answer: Snapshots capture repository and setup changes and can be deleted from settings or CLI.

services.answer: Long-running processes belong in .amp/services.yaml or systemd, not setup.

secrets.answer: Shared setup and runtime use different credentials; setup credentials are removed before snapshotting.

duplicate_installs.answer: A matching project snapshot skips setup; freshness is limited to 72 hours and supported Git host checks.

automatic_repair.answer: .agents/resume runs after activation and wake for authentication, repair or reconnect; successful automatic repair is not independently tested.

timeouts.answer: Setup stops after 20 minutes; a failed or timed-out setup does not publish a refreshed snapshot.

organization_roles.answer: Member and Admin roles are documented; Admin manages membership, billing, settings and policies and can view private threads.

membership.answer: Admins invite members; member email-invitation rights are configurable.

provisioning.answer: Enterprise supports directory sync of members and groups.

plan_scope.answer: A non-enterprise workspace needs a paid Megawatt or Gigawatt member for SAML/OIDC SSO; Enterprise does not require a paid member tier.

actions.answer: Enterprise admins can access authentication event audit logs; comprehensive application audit logs remain internal.

edits.answer: Each artifact save creates a revision and Share identifies the last editing thread agent.

export.answer: Artifacts export to Markdown, HTML or PDF; threads export to Markdown or owner-only JSON.

mutability.answer: Artifacts are editable, with a revision made for each save.

retention.answer: Deleting a thread deletes its artifacts.

integrity.answer: A stale agent artifact write is refused when another revision was saved; the agent must merge its changes.

change_understanding.answer: The Changes pane offers all changes, uncommitted changes or a selected commit.

keyboard.answer: The commit picker supports the right arrow key to read a commit message.

retained_context.answer: Commits carry an Amp-Thread-ID trailer linking a code change back to its conversation.

documents.answer: Thread artifacts retain plans, reports and notes.

gallery.answer: The Artifacts tab groups multiple documents in folders.

task_links.answer: Artifact links in the transcript open the document in its thread.

persistence.answer: Artifacts and their uploaded images remain with the thread; deleting the thread deletes its artifacts.

child_findings.answer: A child thread can edit or copy an accessible parent artifact, then notify its thread of the change.

tests.answer: Default Ship asks the agent to run the full test suite.

failure_blocking.answer: The documented agent instruction ignores a failing test only after confirming that it fails on the base branch too. This describes a prompt, not an independently enforced gate.

configured_policy.answer: A project can configure Ship Behavior or write a Custom Ship prompt.

branches.answer: Push to Branch ships to a feature branch instead of the base branch.

commits.answer: Default Ship commits uncommitted files before rebasing and pushing.

rebase.answer: Default Ship rebases on the latest base branch and repeats after a concurrent push.

conflicts.answer: The agent resolves conflicts and asks the user before proceeding on substantive conflicts.

merge.answer: Default Ship writes directly to the base branch after rebasing; PR approval and merge-policy enforcement are not established.

authority_enforcement.answer: Ship behavior is a project-configured agent prompt. The source does not establish an immutable authorization boundary.

client_license.answer: Amp access is covered by the limited, revocable service license in its custom terms.

server_license.answer: The hosted service is governed by Amp License Terms; an open-source server license was not established.

self_hosting.answer: Amp explicitly says it does not offer self-hosted deployments of its control plane. Self-hosted Orbs are execution workers.

export.answer: Threads export to Markdown, with full JSON available to the creator.

formats.answer: Thread export formats are Markdown and JSON; artifacts export Markdown, HTML and PDF.

history_portability.answer: Thread transcripts can be exported; importing an exported history was not established.

code_data.answer: Local code snippets and context can be sent to Amp Server and model providers.

prompts.answer: Prompts and conversation history are sent to Amp Server and then inference providers.

logs.answer: Authentication audit logs are available to Enterprise admins; internal application logs are not exposed to admins.

retention.answer: Enterprise workspace threads remain until the enterprise contract ends, including after the author leaves.

deletion.answer: Deleting a thread also deletes its associated Orb, usually within seconds.

training.answer: Training can be toggled in Settings Privacy; workspace enabling requires admin approval.

residency.answer: Amp Server stores data in a multi-tenant Google Cloud Platform project; a precise region was not established.

provider_separation.answer: Personal provider subscription terms and data controls apply independently of Amp training settings.

seats.answer: Teams have no extra workspace charge; members retain individual tiers.

workspace_fees.answer: Teams carry no extra charge; Enterprise has custom pricing.

included_usage.answer: Megawatt includes $20 monthly agent usage and 750 hours of a1.small Orbs; larger sizes consume the allowance faster.

credits.answer: Purchased credits expire twelve months after purchase and workspace credits are shared.

overages.answer: Users can buy credits after consuming included agent usage.

model_cost.answer: Own subscriptions and API keys have no Amp fees outside Enterprise; Amp-hosted model credits follow provider prices without markup for non-enterprise users.

soc2_type.answer: Amp publicly states SOC 2 Type II certification; the underlying report was not inspected.

evidence_status.answer: Vendor security statement only; certificate issuer, validity period and report scope were not independently verified.

ongoing_free.answer: The Hobby tier is recurring free; model usage and hosted compute may still cost money.

self_host_cost.answer: Self-hosted Orbs and own subscriptions or API keys have no Amp fee for individuals and teams; infrastructure and provider costs remain.

usage_caps.answer: Hobby includes no usage. Own subscriptions and API keys have no Amp token fees or limits outside Enterprise; provider limits still apply.

units.answer: Agent usage is billed in credits and Orb compute by the minute.

included_limits.answer: Megawatt includes $20 agent usage and 45,000 minutes of a1.small Orbs monthly.

overages.answer: Paid credits permit continued model and tool usage beyond the monthly allowance.

minimum_commitment.answer: Paid credits require no paid tier or commitment.
